newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close sharply lower.

text.p: Light selling attributed to declining cash prices kept CME lumber futures pressured and prices fell as much as the daily limit before ending sharply lower, traders said.
November fell the $10.00 per tbf limit to $339.30 per tbf late before closing $9.90 lower at $339.40. Other months ended $6.70 to $5.20 lower with January off $6.70 at $355.00 per tbf.
Early technical support lacked follow through and futures pushed through the chart point at $340.00 per tbf, basis November, to fall the limit, traders said.
Despite the large discount of futures to cash, futures slipped on selling linked to another large decline in the cash spruce price, they said.

Random Length quoted cash spruce at $382, $10 under midweek levels and $28 under last Friday's quote. The cash spruce price has fallen $50 in the past two weeks and likely will fall another $30, cash sources said.
